A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETCH work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures that can be matched across versions. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original CAPE and 4D-Dress evaluations, component ablations, one-shot experiments, and shape-accuracy results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 6–9.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds challenging-subset comparisons, an invariant-feature ablation, cross-dataset examples, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The equivariant tightness prediction, invariant-feature branches, multitask loss, marker aggregation, and SMPL optimization remain the same. Revised indexing and explanations of multitask training and top-confidence aggregation clarify the existing procedure; they do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 adds reported qualitative transfer tests on THuman2.1 scans and HuGe100K generated humans using a 4D-Dress-trained model (Figure 11), plus partial-point testing (Figure 10). The fitting task and training datasets remain unchanged. The challenging 4D-Dress subsets select cases from existing coverage.

E2.justification: The external comparators remain NICP, ArtEq, IPNet, and PTF. V2 adds Ours-E, using invariant features alone for direction prediction, to the ablation comparison in Table 3. Extending the existing external comparators to Table 2's subsets does not change that comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 introduces top-10% challenge-subset evaluations selected using tightness magnitude, the first three SMPL shape parameters, and pose parameters. It also adds an invariant-only control and cross-dataset testing. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, sampling settings, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Robustness analysis expands substantially through three challenging-subset comparisons (Table 2), the invariant-only ablation (Table 3), illustrated failures involving hands, missing points, and extreme garments (Figure 10), and cross-dataset transfer examples (Figure 11). These supplement the retained component, one-shot, and post-refinement analyses.

E5.justification: The same mean and median directional-error summaries are retained. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 7's error color scale does not represent statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for challenging subsets, Ours-E, transfer, and failures, plus a reported marker error of 0.31% of body scale. New Table 2 reports ETCH V2V errors of 2.276, 1.831, and 1.992 cm across its three subsets; these are additional evaluations, not improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, losses, and optimization objective are retained without new proofs or derivations. Feature indexing and predicted-label notation are clarified. Correcting 'outer' to 'inner' in the description of S_Y resolves terminology consistently with the already-defined body surface, rather than introducing a new mathematical construction.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same novelty, accuracy, and generalization claims, including their headline percentages. The added evaluations provide support for those claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 explains why multitask supervision and Euclidean marker aggregation are preferred, interprets Ours-E as evidence against invariant-only direction prediction, and identifies extremely unusual garments as a failure boundary. Partial-input, thin-structure, and scalability limitations were already discussed in v1.

D1.justification: V2 discloses top-three marker aggregation, specifies selection by confidence within predicted labels, explains canonical-space dense correspondence, and explicitly states that models share the reported data settings. These improve documentation without establishing changed implementation settings. Hardware, training hyperparameters, and promised code availability remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the attribution for confidence aggregation from ArtEq to LoopReg, while Section 3.1 adds an explicit ArtEq citation for rotation-group approximation. Both works were already referenced; the 76-work bibliography and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds focused explanatory paragraphs and experiment descriptions, corrects notation and terminology, and updates affiliation and acknowledgments. The section organization and most existing prose remain intact; this is not an extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adds the challenge-subset table and two figures showing failures and cross-dataset testing, expands the ablation table, and updates its caption. Existing tables are renumbered and several displays relocate, while the overall two-column layout and principal figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the existing generalization evidence with targeted quantitative comparisons in Table 2 and the Ours-E control, while Figure 10 makes failure boundaries concrete. Aggregation and training clarifications also improve reproducibility. These are useful, focused gains; the central method and matched results remain unchanged, and the new cross-dataset evidence is qualitative.
